Session guide
Each person names one thing they use every day. The group votes: AI or not?
Give the group a few examples and ask what a learner would guess. Then show lopsided examples and ask what goes wrong.
Read the red-flag card aloud. For each flag, the group says: go to a health facility now.
Use the five-tricks poster. Read a post aloud and the group names the trick.
Use the check-before-share card. Practise the three steps, then a kind reply.
List tasks at work. The group sorts them: AI can help, or a person must decide.
Describe a picture or video. The group says: made by AI? What label should it have?
Each person shares one habit that keeps them scrolling and one simple boundary.
Name who could be left out of a health app. The group suggests one fix for each.
Read the data rights aloud. Practise who to complain to, step by step.

The 45-minute flow
The core idea: calibrated trust
ARAW does not say "trust nothing". It helps people trust the right things, by the right amount.
End every session with the same question:
Keep everyone safe
Kindness and health safety come first.
Kindness rules
Nobody is shamed or blamed. People share myths because they care.
Mock the trick, never the person.
Talk with people, not down to them. Use plain words and go slowly.
Show what good sources look like, not only what to avoid.
Every answer is welcome. Some prompts have no single right answer.
Health safety rule
Never give doses, diagnoses or treatment advice.
Always point to people: a health worker, the barangay health center or a doctor.
If anyone describes chest pain, trouble breathing, stroke signs, a seizure or heavy bleeding, tell them to go to a health facility now. Do not wait for the session to end.
The red-flag card in this kit lists the signs. Keep it on the table.
